core_obligations: Reduce a fraction integral over the ring to the case where numerator and denominator are coprime (proof lines 8288-8292).
Use an integrality relation to show the whole numerator power lies in the ideal generated by the denominator, which forces the denominator to be a unit (proof lines 8292-8295).
proof_roadmap: Read the contradiction from the integrality relation (proof lines 8292-8296).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a principal ideal domain is normal, that is, integrally closed in its fraction field (statement lines 8282-8285). The proof does not use unique factorization: it cancels the common factor of a fraction to reach the coprime case and then reads an integrality relation as a divisibility statement forcing the denominator to be a unit (proof lines 8287-8296). Using only that the ring is a principal ideal domain, rather than that it is a UFD, is what distinguishes this argument from the general one. H2.
